media_work.title: 60 Minutes
media_work.summaryNotes: Highlighted the role of withheld evidence in a long-term wrongful conviction.

media_item.summary_notes: This 60 Minutes segment reported by Lara Logan highlights the impact of prosecutorial misconduct and withheld evidence on a wrongful conviction.
key_quotes_raw: Archival footage of Anderson mocking Morton's tears during the original trial.
systemic_issues_raw: The devastating impact of prosecutorial misconduct
The difficulty in holding prosecutors accountable
The long battle often required for DNA testing.
policy_recommendations_raw: Implied need for greater prosecutorial accountability
Stricter adherence to evidence disclosure rules (Brady rule).

external_links_raw.description: Accountability Works," Morton Tells "60 Minutes" - The Texas Tribune

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Michael Morton was wrongfully convicted of the murder of his wife in 1987 and spent 25 years in prison. He was exonerated by DNA evidence in 2011 and later received state compensation.
organizations_involved_raw: Innocence Project (instrumental in DNA testing and uncovering withheld evidence).

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: N/A (Later faced investigation/prosecution for misconduct related to the Morton case).
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Ken Anderson was the prosecutor in Michael Morton's case. He faced investigation and potential criminal charges for his role in Morton's wrongful conviction for allegedly withholding exculpatory evidence.
contributing_factors_raw: Allegedly withheld critical exculpatory evidence from the defense.
